task: Land the taste-lint error-count ratchet for issue #3779 and record the retrospective the push gate now requires. The UTC date rolled to 2026-07-30 with the last retrospective dated 2026-07-28, so both the today and yesterday windows in check_retrospective_evidence were bare and the gate blocked every pending push. The retrospective is genuine work, not a gate workaround: this session overturned 82 written premises by measurement and that rate is the finding worth recording.

events.content: Measured the git path-existence contract rather than trusting the review comment. The reviewer stated git cat-file -e returns 1 for a missing path and 128 for a fatal error. On git 2.43.0 in a scratch repository the result is inverted: the ref-and-path form returns 128 for absent, and 1 appears only for a bare well-formed 40-hex object id.

Refuted my own replacement. git rev-parse --verify --quiet collapses both the absent and refused cases to 1, and without --quiet both are 128, so it discriminates in neither direction. My own tests caught this before it shipped.

Built a four-path probe covering present, absent, a relative path escaping the worktree, and an absolute outside path. git ls-tree is the only measured discriminator: rc 0 with non-empty stdout means present, rc 0 with empty stdout means absent, rc 128 means refused. It is a true allowlist, so it fails closed on anything unmeasured.

Confirmed the reviewer's conclusion was right through a mechanism neither of us had named. A baseline path escaping the worktree read as bootstrap and waived the raise check, which is the fail-open row they predicted.

Extracted _git_run so _git_rc delegates to it, then ran 5 mutants. M5 survived because nothing covered git failing to launch on the path probe. Added a test that fails only when the ls-tree leg is removed and all 5 died.

The ratchet caught its own pull request twice. The new test file crossed the 500-line taste-lint ceiling and was split into tests/ci/test_count_ratchet_against_real_git.py. After a rebase the tracked-tree count read 616 against a baseline of 615.

Measured origin/main in a detached scratch worktree rather than assuming I had caused the drift. main itself is at 616. Traced the extra violation to a complexity-12 function I landed the same morning in PR #3799 and extracted two helpers from it instead of raising the baseline, because 615 is also written into the module docstring and the pull request prose.

The push failed on retrospective-policy after every other gate passed. Read scripts/validation/git_hook_policy.py and found check_retrospective_evidence globs .agents/retrospective/ for today and yesterday. The UTC rollover to 2026-07-30 invalidated the 2026-07-28 entry that had been satisfying the yesterday window all session. The gate is correct and the missing artifact was real.

Wrote the retrospective against failure mode class 9 with the evidence inline: four reviewer-stated API contracts wrong when measured, one of my own replacements wrong, one of my own posted replies wrong and publicly corrected, and three of my own theories refuted by data in the same session that produced them.

Hit session-policy on the retrospective commit: staged .agents changes require a JSON session log in the same commit. Wrote this log rather than splitting the commit, which is the behavior that gate is designed to force.
